subject: Pricing qualification & context length profiling
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kate Larson <kate@acmeanalytics.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing qualification & context length profiling

Hi Kate / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we all have the same set of asks and next steps:

What I heard on the call:
- Primary workflows: conversational analytics (customer-facing chat), nightly batch summarization of transcripts, and RAG for long-form reports.
- Initial pilots will be chat-heavy with some heavy batch jobs for summarization.
- There are a few use-cases that may require long context (legal/report retrieval) but most interactions are short.

Qualifying questions / asks (if you can share before our follow-up it'll speed the pricing exercise):
1) Rough monthly token volumes (or a range) for pilot and for 12-month target.
2) Target unit economics (target $/1M tokens) or monthly budget range for inference.
3) Avg prompt tokens and avg completion tokens (or examples we can sample).
4) Percent of requests that need >8k, >32k and >128k context (ballpark okay).
5) Any SLA/latency constraints or peak concurrency concerns.

Why this matters: the mix of prompt vs completion tokens and the fraction of long-context requests is what drives model choice, batching strategy, and ultimately the $/1M tokens we can achieve. With those numbers we can produce a 2–3 price scenarios: hosted (pay-as-you-go), reserved/dedicated (committed capacity), and an optimized dedicated plan with batching/quantization assumptions.

Next steps:
- Kate: if you can share the numbers above and a handful of anonymized example prompts/completions, Laura will do a quick context-length profile and give a sizing recommendation.
- Vivek / Laura / me: we’ll produce a short pricing model and a recommended config (model family, context length tiers, estimated $/1M tokens) and circulate a draft SOW.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0128

From: Kate Larson <kate@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Reed <tom.reed@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing qualification & context length profiling

Thanks Aditya — good summary. A few answers and clarifications below (ballpark numbers to start):

- Monthly volume: Pilot expected ~200–300M tokens/month. 12-month target (if pilot converts + growth): ~2.0–2.5B tokens/month.
- Budget & unit economics: For procurement, our internal target is roughly $10–$25 per 1M tokens depending on SLA and feature set (security/compliance). Traffic/volume that hits the 12-month target would push us toward the lower end, pilot budget is limited (~$8k–$12k/mo).
- Avg token breakdown (approx): avg prompt tokens: 180 tokens; avg completion tokens: 620 tokens — total ~800 tokens per request.
- Context-length needs: ~85% of requests are within 8k, ~12% require 32k, and ~3% would need 128k occasionally (monthly spikes for large legal/report retrieval).
- Peak concurrency: typical peak concurrency is modest (20–50 qps), but we have spike windows during morning report runs where we could see short bursts up to ~200 qps for a few minutes.
- Compliance: must support SOC2 + customer contract redaction on request.

We can provide a small sample (10–20) of anonymized prompts and completions and a histogram export of token sizes by next week.

On pricing, our procurement team prefers unit economics in $/1M tokens to be surfaced so they can compare to other vendors; target for us is to get to ~$15–$18/1M tokens for production (with dedicated/commit discounts available).

Best,
Kate Larson
Head of Product — Analytics Platform

Thanks, Kate — this is really helpful. A few technical follow-ups that will help us produce an accurate pricing model and context-tier recommendation: 

1) Request split by use-case: can you give a % split for chat vs batch summarization vs RAG (e.g., 70/20/10)?
2) For the 3% that need 128k, are these single requests (one large doc) or multi-request sessions where you stitch results?
3) Please share a small sample of prompts/completions and a token-size histogram (CSV). If you can’t share real content, synthetic examples with similar token-length distribution are fine.

Ballpark economics we’ll use to produce scenarios (we’ll adjust once we see samples):
- Hosted (no commit): assume list-tier $/1M tokens for 8k-friendly models (this is a reference point).
- Dedicated / committed: with 12+ month commit and predictable volumes, we can typically model down to ~$8–$12 / 1M tokens through reserved capacity, batching, and quantization for the majority 8k workload.
- Mixed-tier: given ~12% 32k and ~3% 128k, we’ll recommend a blended approach: primary dedicated pool for 8k workload + on-demand higher-context instances for 32k/128k spikes. That tends to hit both unit-economics and availability targets.

Notes on sizing: with your ~800 tokens per request average and projected 2B tokens/month, we’d model ~2.5M infer calls/month (depending on distribution). Batching and prefix caching on repeated prompts can materially reduce effective tokens/second for cost.

If you can share samples by EOD Thursday, I’ll run a quick profiler and send a short spreadsheet with: estimated per-tier cost ($/1M tokens), recommended model sizes, and a suggested committed capacity commit level.

– Laura
